# The halite Handbook

<!-- Generated by tools/handbook. Edit the code, not this file. -->

This directory is the handbook: a complete guide to halite for someone who has never
seen it, from what it is and why, through writing and running a fleet's configuration,
to the runbooks for operating it, the reference, and the code. It is part of every
release (the archives carry it as HTML and Markdown), and the tests that keep it
honest are described in the chapter on how it is built.

To read it as a book, open `index.html` from the handbook directory of a release
archive, or build it with `make handbook` and open `build/handbook/index.html`. The
index is `genindex.html`, and `handbook.html` is the whole book on one page.

## Orientation

- 1. [What halite is](01-what-is-halite.md) — The problem halite solves, what you get from it, what it is not, and how to read this handbook.
- 2. [The concepts in one sitting](02-concepts.md) — The vocabulary and the mental model: nodes, the hub, states, grains, pillar, jobs, events, and how a change travels.
- 3. [A guided tour](03-guided-tour.md) — Ten minutes, one machine, no server: describe a machine, rehearse the change, apply it, apply it again, and watch drift being repaired.

## Describing machines

- 4. [Idempotency and convergence](04-idempotency.md) — The idea everything else rests on: declare an end state, change only what differs, do nothing when already correct.
- 5. [States and SLS files](05-states.md) — The language you describe machines in: YAML declarations, IDs, arguments, include and extend, options, and how to run and inspect them.
- 6. [Requisites and ordering](06-requisites.md) — How states depend on each other: require, watch, onchanges, onfail, prereq, use, listen, the _in forms, and the rules that decide the final order.
- 7. [Templates](07-templates.md) — Jinja inside SLS files and delivered files: the syntax, the names available, loops, macros, imports, filters, strict undefined, and debugging.
- 8. [Grains](08-grains.md) — The facts a node knows about itself, how to read them, how to add your own, and why you must not trust them with secrets.
- 9. [Pillar](09-pillar.md) — Per-node data and secrets: how pillar is written, targeted, merged and protected, and what it does and does not do.
- 10. [The top file, environments and the file server](10-top-and-files.md) — How a tree is laid out and served: the top file that assigns states to nodes, environments, file roots, git and S3 backends, and good tree structure.
- 11. [The module library](11-modules.md) — What halite can manage: execution and state modules, how to discover them, virtual modules and providers, the evidence levels, and where the library ends.

## Acting on the fleet

- 12. [The hub and its nodes](12-hub-and-nodes.md) — How the control plane and the agents connect: the one port, the persistent connection, what lives where on disk, and what happens when either side goes away.
- 13. [Targeting](13-targeting.md) — Choosing the nodes a command, a state or a rule applies to: globs, lists, regular expressions, grains, pillar, subnets, nodegroups and compound expressions.
- 14. [Remote execution](14-remote-execution.md) — Running functions and states on many machines from the hub: arguments, output, exit codes, batching, canaries, asynchronous jobs and offline nodes.
- 15. [Jobs and the job cache](15-jobs.md) — What a job is, how it is recorded, how to look one up afterwards, and how long the record lasts.
- 16. [Configuration management at scale](16-fleet-operations.md) — Running a tree against a whole fleet: how changes flow from git to machines, scheduling, drift reports, rollouts, promotion and failure handling.
- 17. [Agentless mode](17-agentless.md) — Managing machines that run no halite agent, over SSH: the roster, what is pushed, what works, and what cannot.

## Automation

- 18. [The event bus](18-events.md) — The stream of everything that happens: tags, payloads, listening, replaying, sending, and the rules that stop a node from forging the control plane's events.
- 19. [Beacons](19-beacons.md) — Watchers on the node that put an event on the bus when something changes: configuration, every built beacon with real output, the loop-prevention controls, and runtime management.
- 20. [Reactors](20-reactors.md) — Rules that turn events into actions on the hub: configuration, reaction files, the four reaction types, authorization as a principal, rate and loop controls, and how to test one before it fires.
- 21. [Orchestration](21-orchestration.md) — Multi-step, multi-machine procedures that run on the hub: step types, ordering and rollback with requisites, batches, waiting for events, rehearsal, and resuming a failed run.
- 22. [Runners and the mine](22-runners-and-mine.md) — Functions that run on the hub rather than on a node, every runner this build ships, and the mine: how nodes publish facts for other nodes to read.
- 23. [The scheduler and returners](23-scheduler-and-returners.md) — Work on a timetable, run by the node itself; and where results and events go: local files, syslog, mail and signed webhooks with a durable spool.
- 24. [Scenarios: putting it together](24-scenarios.md) — Whole procedures built from the parts: a file that repairs itself, a node that onboards itself, a certificate that raises its own alarm, a rollout that waits for a human.

## Security and identity

- 25. [Trust and identity](25-trust-and-identity.md) — How a node proves who it is: the enrollment CA, fingerprint pinning, manual and token enrollment, certificate lifetimes and renewal, revocation, and what each key protects.
- 26. [Authentication and authorization](26-authorization.md) — Who may do what: principals, the one policy file, roles and rules with target, function and argument limits, the functions no wildcard grants, and how to test a policy before it matters.
- 27. [The HTTP API](27-http-api.md) — Driving halite from other software: logging in, running functions and states, jobs, nodes, events as a stream, webhook ingress, and how the API is bounded by the policy.
- 28. [Hardening: signing, the sandbox and evidence](28-hardening.md) — The controls that limit what a compromised part can do: signed jobs, the render sandbox, unprivileged accounts, signed trees, the node's evidence chain, FIPS, and a checklist.
- 29. [Extensions](29-extensions.md) — How halite is extended without ever loading code into the agent: signed bundles run as separate processes, the kinds, the trust and pinning model, and the commands to build, check, sign and publish one.

## Runbooks

- 30. [Runbook: installing a hub](30-install-hub.md) — Standing up the control plane on Linux or FreeBSD: verify, install, configure, start, make yourself an operator, and prove it works.
- 31. [Runbook: installing and enrolling nodes](31-install-nodes.md) — Putting the agent on a machine and bringing it into the fleet: one node by hand, many with tokens, and what to do about images.
- 32. [Runbook: installing the API and giving people access](32-install-api.md) — Running halite-api in front of the hub: its two certificates, its policy role, the service, accounts and tokens, and handing out access safely.
- 33. [Runbook: configuring halite](33-configuration.md) — Where configuration lives on each platform, how files and drop-ins combine, the settings you will actually change, how to change them safely, and how to manage halite's own configuration with halite.
- 34. [Runbook: monitoring and alerting](34-monitoring.md) — What to watch and how: doctor for health, Prometheus metrics from the API and nodes, the numbers that answer most questions, alert rules, logs, the event stream and a dashboard.
- 35. [Runbook: backup, restore and disaster recovery](35-backup-and-recovery.md) — What to back up on a hub and a node, how to restore a hub without re-enrolling anyone, and what losing each piece actually costs, with the failure shown.
- 36. [Runbook: upgrading and rolling back](36-upgrades.md) — Moving a hub, an API and a fleet of nodes to a new release: verify, read, back up, canary, roll, confirm, and how to go back.
- 37. [Runbook: certificate operations](37-certificates.md) — Every certificate in the estate, who renews it, how to see how long it has, how to renew or replace each, and how to plan for the one thing that does not renew: the CA.
- 38. [Runbook: sizing, scaling and relays](38-scaling.md) — How big a hub needs to be, what has and has not been measured, the knobs that matter, and how to add a relay for a distant or isolated segment.
- 39. [Troubleshooting guide](39-troubleshooting.md) — A method for finding what is wrong, then a catalogue of the symptoms halite actually produces, with the real message, the cause and the fix.
- 40. [Runbook: incident playbooks](40-incidents.md) — What to do, in order, when a node, a credential, a rollout, a reactor or the hub itself goes wrong: contain first, then investigate, then recover.
- 41. [Runbook: migrating a Salt estate](41-migrating.md) — The staged path from an existing Salt estate: audit the tree, stand up halite beside it, prove one machine, widen, switch off, and what is different on the way.
